name: Scuba diving courses
summary: How expats choose PADI/SSI diving courses in Singapore and nearby — pool confins, medical forms, and weekend trip logistics — without confusing discovery dives with certification that transfers worldwide.
body:
Singapore is a training hub with pool sessions locally and open-water weekends on nearby islands or further afield. Expats often start with Discover Scuba, then Open Water, Advanced, and rescue tracks through PADI, SSI, or other agencies.

## Course realities
- Classroom / e-learning + confined pool + open-water dives
- Medical questionnaire — some answers require physician sign-off before in-water
- Gear hire vs buy; humid storage and servicing matter
- Certification cards should be verifiable online with the agency

A resort “resort diver” experience is not a substitute for full Open Water if you want portable certification.

## Safety culture
Ask about instructor ratios, current briefings, and emergency oxygen/ first-aid readiness. Cheap packages that skip pool time or rush medical screening are not bargains. Equalise patiently — forcing ears ruins trips.

## How to choose
Prefer shops with clear course calendars, published referral policies if weather cancels boats, and gear that fits a range of body sizes. Check whether weekends conflict with school CCAs for families. For kids’ junior programmes, confirm age minimums and supervision rules.

## Practical tip
Complete e-learning before the pool weekend so you are not cramming theory after a full work week. If you take medication or have asthma/ear issues, sort the dive medical early — last-minute GP letters on Saturday mornings are miserable.
